calls.title: Ikea + GrowthBook
calls.summary: IKEA is currently spending over €1 million annually on Optimizely, with a contract extending through July 2027. The platform's usability challenges prompted IKEA to develop a custom frontend for better experiment management. With an average of 16.5 to 17 million monthly active users and 571 seats in use, IKEA intends to expand its seat count to enhance its experimentation culture. Growth Book is positioned as a potential alternative, proposing a seat-based pricing model that could halve IKEA's costs, along with flexible transition options. The procurement process will involve vendor comparisons and board-level approvals, with plans for proof of concept trials to guide their decision-making.
calls.keywords: Experimentation, Optimizely, GrowthBook, Pricing Model, BigQuery, Procurement

Christian will provide a written summary of GrowthBook's agentic AI vision and differentiation, and arrange a customer reference call within weeks, while Cecilia continues internal market research and demos.

calls.title: IKEA + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The discussion centered on IKEA's ambition to enhance its experimentation capabilities, aiming for an annual target of 1,500 to 2,000 experiments, up from around 500 currently. The focus was on prioritizing experiment quality and safety to avoid costly incidents, utilizing tools like feature flags. AI integration was highlighted as a critical leverage point to increase efficiency and enhance ROI across the experimentation lifecycle. Two pricing models were proposed by GrowthBook, both priced around $871,000 annually, offering flexible options for IKEA to evaluate. Additionally, operational risks related to infrastructure and uncertain BigQuery costs were acknowledged, along with an emphasis on the partnership, which aims to be a long-term strategic collaboration, ensuring adaptability in IKEA’s evolving needs.
calls.keywords: Experimentation, Pricing Models, AI Integration, Feature Flags, RFP Proposal, Reliability Risks
